transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE); Daniel Rios (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (CloudWell Head of Platform); Ethan Brooks (CloudWell VP Eng); Sofia Martinez (Cloud Ops)

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in to discuss retainer top-up, add eu region onramp, and align on private benchmark and updated SOW. Heavy focus on latency targets, KMS/SSO details and peak-hour footprint.

Topics:
- Retainer uplift sizing and tiers
- Multi-region activation (eu-west)
- Private pilot and latency benchmarking
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
- Contract amendment timeline and legal touchpoints

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for jumpin in. um quick agenda, retainer top-up, eu onramp, and a short benchmark plan. Priya, Ethan, you good with that?
[00:12] Priya: yeah that's perfect. we wanted to get this aligned before next sprint so ops can plan.
[00:20] Ethan: also want to confirm numbers — our traffic's spiky end of month, roughly 1.6M tokens/day now, with peaks around 11pm UTC.
[00:30] Sofia: mm-hmm, and some of the nights we get double the base for about an hour.
[00:37] Daniel: cool, that helps. our suggestion is a retainer uplift to cover baseline plus a burst buffer, so you don't pay full on-demand for peak churning.
[00:49] Priya: can you walk through the tiers again? last time the doc had quantization options and shared/dedicated pools and we got a bit lost.
[00:58] Maya: sure, so two main levers: Dedicated pool (predictable throughput, reserved GPUs) and Hosted with smart routing + KV cache. for your use case we recommended a Dedicated baseline for critical routes and hosted fallback for non-critical traffic.
[01:15] Ethan: the dedicated pool — does that require new network peering or is it all over the redwood console?
[01:22] Daniel: no new peering by default. for Private/VPC deployments you'd do a VP C peering — pardon, VPC — but Dedicated in our hosted offering sits behind our secure fabric. we can also provision a VPC connector if you want direct egress.
[01:38] Sofia: we will need VPC and KMS integration, we can't have keys outside our KMS.
[01:44] Maya: understood. we have KMS/HSM integrations; we'll share the KMS playbook. you'll need to confirm whether it's AWS KMS or customer-managed HSM for the private pilot.
[01:56] Priya: AWS KMS, but we want the HSM conversation open. legal will probably push for customer-managed keys.
[02:05] Daniel: noted. for the eu activation, we usually do a phased onramp: stage traffic, run lat bench, validate cache hit rates, then flip. benchmark plan will include cold starts, kv cash (sic) warmup, and long-seq token churn.
[02:25] Ethan: what's realistic latency for the eu-region once it's live? our SLO target is p95 <= 220ms for short completions (<=64 tokens).
[02:34] Daniel: p95 ~180-240ms depending on model variant and sequence length; with continuous batching and prefix caching we can hit mid-200s for the 13B style models. if you quantize to int8 we see slight improves but with a small quality delta.
[02:55] Priya: what about cost delta with quantization? we don't want regressions in reply quality for customer-facing flows.
[03:02] Maya: our Optimize team provides recommended quant profiles per route. we can run A/B quality comparisons during the benchmark and tag regressions to prompt sets you provide.
[03:14] Sofia: ok and the private pilot: how long until we can run it? we need real numbers for procurement.
[03:20] Daniel: typical schedule is two weeks prep and a two-day run — so about 3 weeks overall to get meaningful results. we can compress if you give the traffic samples and whip up the staging config.
[03:33] Ethan: procurement also wants to know the amendment wording — auto-renew vs term extension, and do we get a discount for committing to 12 months?
[03:42] Maya: yes, the SOW amendment will show tiered discounts for 6/12/24 month retainer commitments. we'll send a pricing worksheet with line items for Dedicated baseline, burst units, region activation, and optional private onprem packaging.
[03:58] Priya: great. also, audit logs and retention — we need 13 months for audit, and logs must be exportable to our SIEM.
[04:08] Daniel: our console provides token-level trace and per-route logs. can export to S3 or push to your SIEM via secure delivery. we'll double-check retention parity with your compliance team.
[04:20] Sofia: are there any gotchas with EU data residency? we want model inference data to stay in the eu cluster, not routed back to us-west for fallback.
[04:29] Maya: routing policies can pin by customer and model variant; during eu onramp we'll enforce eu-only routing. fallback policies can be set to fail closed or to fallback to a private variant — we'll document the default.
[04:43] Ethan: what's the downtime risk during region flip?
[04:47] Daniel: zero planned downtime. we do canary rollouts with traffic mirroring then cutover. if capacity is constrained we have fallback to hosted smaller models but that's a controlled degradations path.
[04:59] Priya: on the benchmark specifics — Daniel, can you log KV cache hit rates? we run a lot of multi-turn sessions and cache behavior is critical.
[05:07] Daniel: yes, we emit hit/miss metrics and per-route KV stats; we'll include that in the bench report.
[05:15] Sofia: one more on security: SSO/SAML, RBAC in the console, and audit trails for token usage — can you send the exact SOC2 artifact names we need to reference?
[05:26] Maya: we have a SOC2 pack, ISO stuff, and detailed RBAC doc. I'll attach those to the follow-up e-mail.
[05:34] Ethan: competitor note — AltServe offered us a flat egress rebate but with higher token costs. we're balancing cost vs latency and a more predictable SLA.
[05:45] Maya: that's helpful to know — our retainer model focuses on unit economics and predictable ops.
[05:50] Priya: ok next steps, action items?
[05:53] Maya: I'll recap: Maya sends pricing & SOW draft; Daniel runs bench plan and needs your traffic CSV and a set of eval prompts; Priya confirms KMS preference; Sofia provides traffic profile. legal review week of 7/19.
[06:08] Ethan: sound good. any open questions from anyone?
[06:12] Sofia: just one small ask — can the bench include a simulated double-peak night to see burst tail behavior?
[06:18] Daniel: yes we'll run a synthetic spike and observe queueing, batch sizes, and latency tail.
[06:25] Priya: and include monitoring dashboards so our SREs can see the same graphs.
[06:30] Maya: we'll provide dashboard links and dashboard-as-code snippets for Grafana.
[06:36] Daniel: also we'll test the model variant fallback logic in the staging so you're not surprised.
[06:42] Ethan: timeline again: pricing by 7/12, bench plan by 7/16, bench run start 7/20, legal review week 7/19 — works for us.
[06:53] Maya: perfect. we'll loop in legal and solutions on the thread. thanks everyone.

(Transcript contains occasional mis-transcribed words — e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache; "VP C" for VPC — please refer to attached recording for verbatim audio if needed.)
